impact:
commitArtifact calls assertNotSymlink(fs, targetPath, kind !== "manifest") immediately before fs.rename (src/snapshot/store.ts:2393), commented as closing the symlink-swap race for manifest.json, generation files and pin files. No test ever plants a symlink at a commit target before calling publishSnapshot or createPin.

Deleting the guard, or its throw, would not fail a single test. That is exactly the condition T-009 spent a session proving is invisible to both static review and a green suite: eleven of thirteen receipt guards had never been observed to refuse anything. The same sweep is warranted here — disable each refusal in store.ts one at a time and see which survive.

## EVIDENCE CORRECTED 2026-08-05 — the two counts this issue cited were wrong; the FINDING is unchanged and is in fact stronger

Re-verified against the current tree during the T-011 unpark audit. Recording the correction rather than leaving it, because a stale number inside an open issue is how a filed claim quietly becomes a hypothesis nobody rechecks — which is this project's own lesson about reproducing an issue's evidence before acting on it.

WRONG AS FILED:
- "`grep -c SnapshotPathError tests-ts/snapshot-store.test.mjs` returns 0" — it returns 16.
- "the three 'symlink' hits in the suite" — there are 63.

Neither correction rescues the guard, and the reason is more specific than the original wording implied. The suite's SnapshotPathError assertions that look like commit-target coverage match the message `was replaced between staging and commit` (tests at :737, :3189, :4831, :4885). That message is emitted by **assertStagingIdentity** (store.ts:2480), a DIFFERENT guard protecting a different object — the staging entry, not the commit target. The suite's own comment at :4466 says so: "Armed by `assertStagingIdentity`, which is the LAST filesystem call before the rename".

ALSO WRONG, and found only on the second pass: the original's flat assertion that "no test ever plants a symlink at a commit target before calling publishSnapshot" is FALSE. tests-ts/snapshot-store.test.mjs:245 is a publish test whose case list at :255 does exactly that — `["a symlinked manifest", (fs) => { fs.nodes.delete(P.manifest); fs.symlink(P.manifest, "/outside/x"); }]` — and then calls publishSnapshot.

The finding survives that, and the accurate statement is STRONGER than the original: a symlink IS planted at the manifest commit target, but the publish refuses EARLIER, at the guarded live-manifest read, throwing SnapshotStoreResetError long before commitArtifact is reached. So assertNotSymlink is still never exercised — not because nothing sets up the scenario, but because an earlier guard shadows it. A test that appears to cover the write-side defence is in fact measuring a different one, which is precisely the shape that makes this invisible. The other two symlink-planting sites were checked as well (:1688 FOREIGN_ENTRIES classification, :6632 the GC foreign-entry test); neither is a commit target for a publish or pin in flight.

The sharper measurement, which is the one that should have been filed:
- assertNotSymlink (store.ts:2506) emits exactly two messages of its own: `<path> is a symlink` and `<path> appeared before the commit; this artifact kind is single-use and a rename would replace it`.
- `grep -c "appeared before the commit" tests-ts/snapshot-store.test.mjs` returns **0**.
- No test asserts the commit-target `is a symlink` refusal either. (:247, cited in an earlier draft of this correction as "the one line mentioning a symlinked manifest", is neither the only one nor read-side: it is a comment INSIDE the publish test above, describing readGuarded on the publish path.)

So the write-side symlink-swap defence is never observed to fire, and the tests that superficially cover it are measuring the staging-identity guard instead — the more dangerous shape, because it reads as coverage. Note also that the guard's own doc comment (store.ts:2500-2505) already concedes a residual rename-window that only a link(2) commit primitive would close; that residual is acknowledged and tracked separately, and is not what this issue is about. This issue is about the guard that DOES exist never being exercised.

Not T-011's to fix; it belongs with the T-010 store hardening sweep.
title: [T-010] The write-side symlink-swap defence is never observed to fire
